gloss: to get carried away, to push one's luck

definitions.gloss: to get carried away, to push one's luck, to get cocky
definitions.explanation: To become overconfident or presumptuous after initial success or favorable treatment, often leading to behavior that others find annoying.

examples.japanese: ⟦{褒|ほ}められて→褒める：01204_homeru⟧{図|ず}に{乗|の}るな。
examples.english: Don't get carried away just because you were praised.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{少|すこ}し→少し：00596_sukoshi⟧⟦{成功|せいこう}する→成功する：21445_seikousuru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦すぐ→すぐ：00814_sugu⟧{図|ず}に{乗|の}る。
examples.english: He gets cocky as soon as he has a little success.

examples.japanese: ⟦{上司|じょうし}→上司：03286_joushi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{気|き}→気：02199_ki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{入|い}られて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧⟦からといって→からといって：30623_karatoitte⟧、{図|ず}に{乗|の}って⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{嫌|きら}われる→嫌う：02048_kirau⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
examples.english: If you get carried away just because the boss likes you, people will start to dislike you.

notes:
USAGE:
This expression has a negative connotation and is often used as a warning or criticism. It describes someone who takes advantage of a favorable situation and becomes presumptuous.

ETYMOLOGY:
⟦{図|ず}→図：03368_zu⟧ here refers to a plan or scheme going well. ⟦{乗|の}る→乗る：00511_noru⟧ means to ride or get on. So the expression literally means 'riding on one's successful plan,' implying overconfidence.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{調子|ちょうし}→調子：03491_choushi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}る→乗る：00511_noru⟧ (to get carried away, to get on a roll)
- ⟦{天狗|てんぐ}→天狗：06522_tengu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (to become conceited)
